bibl.title: Time cells in the hippocampus: a new dimension for mapping memories

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: whether hippocampal neurons code elapsed time as a dimension in its own right, and how that coding relates to spatial coding
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the firing properties of time cells parallel those of place cells point for point, so time is an additional dimension integrated with spatial mapping rather than a separate system
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: existence
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Slowly evolving cortical temporal-context signals select among preconfigured intra-hippocampal firing chains, so that a given chain comes to represent a particular temporally organised memory
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Cortical areas of the 'where' stream deliver temporal-context signals to the hippocampus, which then parses that continuous context into discrete time fields
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Repeated sequential activation strengthens connections so each place cell is driven by an earlier-firing cell, producing the backward expansion of place fields
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: temporal information generated in the cerebral cortex and other brain areas may provide signals to time cells, or the phenomenon may arise from firing chains generated locally within the hippocampal circuitry
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the chaining account is supported by place fields expanding backwards from their centre with repeated runs, as if each cell were driven by an earlier-firing one
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the proposed resolution is a slowly evolving temporal context selecting among preconfigured firing chains, rather than either alone
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: prefrontal and parietal areas of the where stream turn out to be involved in the perception of time and project strongly to the hippocampus
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The origin of hippocampal timing signals - external input versus internally generated firing chains - is left unresolved.
span.note: what this limits: any mechanistic reading of time cells: IT REMAINS A CENTRAL QUESTION WHETHER TEMPORAL INFORMATION ... ORIGINATES FROM ITS INPUTS OR IS GENERATED INTERNALLY
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The evidence reviewed is almost entirely restricted to hippocampal area CA1.
span.note: what this limits: the anatomical reach of the whole review: STUDIES OF TIME CELLS HAVE FOCUSED ON HIPPOCAMPAL AREA CA1 BECAUSE THIS AREA SEEMS TO BE THE MOST IMPORTANT FOR TEMPORAL ORGANIZATION
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The temporal/spatial distinction may be superficial if both reduce to association by proximity.
span.note: what this limits: the time/space distinction the review is built on: IT REMAINS ENTIRELY POSSIBLE THAT THE COMMON THREAD IN BOTH DIMENSIONS IS 'ASSOCIATION BY PROXIMITY' IN SPACE OR TIME
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: whether the temporal signal comes from the inputs, is generated internally, or both, is left as the central open question
span.note: duplicate of: limitations[0] · what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - inputs, internal generation, or a combination, all still open
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: one study reports new temporal patterns emerging with learning rather than existing chains being co-opted, against the preconfigured account
span.note: what this limits: the co-opted-chains account specifically: one study Quotation withheld
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the human recordings show slowly changing patterns rather than the punctate time-cell activations seen in rodents, so the cross-species claim rests on a phenomenon of different form
span.note: what this limits: the human-to-rodent join: the human patterns MORE CLOSELY RESEMBLE THE GRADUALLY EVOLVING TIME SIGNAL ... THAN THE SEQUENCES OF PUNCTATE TIME-CELL ACTIVATIONS in rodents, and are still read as the same phenomenon
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: studies of time cells have focused on hippocampal area CA1, with some evidence for CA2 but not CA3
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 1, with what is known outside CA1: THERE IS SOME EVIDENCE THAT AREA CA2 (BUT NOT CA3) COULD ALSO BE IMPORTANT FOR TEMPORAL PROCESSING
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the author's closing possibility is that time cells and place cells are both reflections of association by proximity, which would dissolve the distinction the review is built on
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 2, with the consequence spelled out: PLACE CELLS AND TIME CELLS ARE SIMPLY REFLECTIONS OF A BASIC FUNCTION OF THE HIPPOCAMPUS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the cue-and-structure vocabulary carried over term by term: temporal cues answering to spatial cues, temporal structure to spatial structure
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: scalar timing, imported as the criterion a neural code must satisfy to count as a code for time
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: time cell and place cell are two names for ONE population - the same neurons, distinguished by which dimension the experiment lets you measure, not by which cells they are
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the parallel is term for term, not loose analogy: temporal cues answer to spatial cues, temporal structure to spatial structure, re-timing to re-mapping, time fields to place fields
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the name 'time cell' is a coinage of one particular study, made on the strength of an analogy to place cells - because they fire at moments as place cells fire at locations - rather than on a mechanism
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: scalar coding - later cells firing for longer - is not decoration but the property that adjudicates between the two mechanisms, since uniform-duration chains cannot produce it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: temporal coding in humans means gradually changing population patterns, while in rodents it means punctate successive activations; the review says so while treating both as the same finding
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: judging an interval and remembering temporal organisation are separated, with the hippocampus central only to the second - so 'timing' names two roles with different anatomy
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: phenomenon: hippocampal neurons firing at successive specific moments within a temporally structured period, filling it out
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: hippocampal time cells — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.

span.label: contradicts → the view that the fundamental function of the hippocampus is spatial mapping and navigation (the paper's reference 75)
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: builds-on → the scalar temporal context model (the paper's reference 69)
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: contradicts → the view that the fundamental function of the hippocampus is spatial mapping and navigation
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: critiques → the strict chaining model in which time cells are a single fixed sequence of cell activations
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: builds-on → the temporal context model of hippocampal coding, in its scalar variant
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: qualifies → the original reports of hippocampal temporal coding, criticised as confounded by location and distance travelled
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS A SPATIAL CONFOUND. The original temporal-coding reports 'were initially CRITICIZED AS BEING CONFOUNDED BY EFFECTS OF VARIATIONS IN THE ANIMAL'S LOCATION ACROSS TIME and of distance travelled over time, so that THE APPARENT TEMPORAL CODING COULD REFLECT SPATIAL rathe[r than temporal] coding'. The finding is not denied - an alternative explanation for it is offered, on one named variable. Q-443.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: extends → the place-cell account of hippocampal function, by adding a temporal dimension carried by the same cells
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: time cells —same-as→ place cells
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — THE STRONGEST SAME-AS IN THE CORPUS: not two populations but one, given two names by two literatures. No lexical join could find this
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: time cells —contrasted-with→ place cells
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.6 — the record marks this weak — and yet they are systematically OPPOSED term by term - temporal cues against spatial cues, temporal structure against spatial structure. Same cells, mirrored vocabularies
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: re-time —same-as→ re-map
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — one process under two names, and the review states the parallel explicitly rather than leaving it to be noticed
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: scalar coding —operationalised-as→ time-fields
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — scalar time is read off the width of the field, not off any clock
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: firing chains —contrasted-with→ temporal context
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — CRITERION: uniform-duration chains cannot produce later cells that fire longer, and scalar firing is what the temporal context model predicts
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: temporal context —contrasted-with→ chaining model
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — external source against internal generation - the two candidate origins the review is organised around
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: temporal context —causes→ firing chains
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — the proposed resolution: context SELECTS among chains rather than either mechanism acting alone. A proposal, hedged as 'perhaps the most likely' - weighted accordingly
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: elapsed time —distinct-from→ distance travelled
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — DECOUPLED BY DESIGN: treadmill speed varied randomly per trial so the two could be separated at all
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: distance travelled —contrasted-with→ elapsed time
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — AND THE CONFOUND SURVIVED: most cells encoded BOTH, to differing degrees - decoupling vindicated the variable without eliminating the rival
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: treadmill —operationalised-as→ elapsed time
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: general linear model —operationalised-as→ elapsed time
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — time is what is left after head position and distance are taken out - a residual, not a direct measurement
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: head-fixed —operationalised-as→ time cells
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — the last rung of the ladder - remove location and movement entirely rather than model them
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: grid cells —part-of→ entorhinal cortex
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — and they too fire at particular moments, so the same dual coding appears one synapse upstream
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: CA1 —contrasted-with→ CA2
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.7 — SCOPE: nearly all the evidence is CA1; CA2 has some support and CA3 explicitly none
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: parietal areas —causes→ hippocampus
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — areas classed with the spatial stream turn out to be involved in the perception of time, and they project strongly here - the stream's NAME is itself the problem. The quote says 'suggest', so this is an inference about routing, not a demonstrated path
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: association by proximity —distinct-from→ time cells
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.6 — the record marks this weak — THE AUTHOR'S OWN DEFLATION: if the common thread is proximity, then time cells and place cells are both epiphenomena of one associative function
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: trace eye-blink conditioning —distinct-from→ firing chains
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHETHER LEARNING CREATES THE PATTERN OR RECRUITS ONE. 'one study examining trace eye-blink conditioning Quotation withheld.' Both accounts predict temporally structured firing after learning and differ only on where the structure came from - which is invisible in the trained animal and visible only across learning. Q-466. · strength of the relation: 0.8 — the dissenting paradigm: new patterns EMERGED with learning rather than existing chains being co-opted
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Hippocampal CA1 principal cells encode the temporal structure of remembered experience independently of the animal's location and movement.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Time cells and place cells are not distinct populations — the same hippocampal neurons carry both codes.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Time-cell firing sequences emerge with learning, are specific to particular memories, and predict whether a subsequent memory judgement will be correct.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A strict chaining account of time cells is rejected, chiefly because elongating a delay makes cells re-time rather than simply lengthening a chain, and because chains cannot split to disambiguate overlapping memories.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The prevalence of temporal coding argues against a purely spatial-navigation account of hippocampal function in favour of organising experience in both space and time.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the original temporal-coding reports were criticised as confounded by the animal's changing location and by distance travelled over time
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: later studies addressed this by tightly controlling the animal's location and movement
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: FIRST RUNG: cells with reliable place fields were simply excluded from the analysis
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: SECOND RUNG: a general linear model separated location, speed and head direction from elapsed time, leaving an independent contribution of time
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THIRD RUNG, THE DECOUPLING: treadmill speed was randomised per trial so that elapsed time and distance travelled could be disentangled
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: over 80 percent of active neurons were modulated by elapsed time, position mattered little, but distance was also strongly encoded and most cells carried both
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: FOURTH RUNG: head-fixed preparations removed location and movement altogether
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the conclusion the ladder licenses: CA1 principal cells encode temporal structure independently of location and movement
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AN EARLY DISSOCIATION: spatial representations differed across trials too, but equally on correct and error trials, so they did not predict memory accuracy
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the firing patterns of many neurons re-timed when the delay was increased, even though the behaviour and locations of the animal during the initial period did not change
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: cells firing later in the delay were active for longer, a scalar coding of time paralleling human and animal time judgements

span.label: THE IDENTITY CLAIM: time cells are the same neurons as place cells, and in freely moving animals fire only when the animal is in a particular location
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the same cells that fired at particular moments on the treadmill fired at particular places on the maze outside it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the reorganisation of time cells when a temporal cue changes parallels the reorganisation of place cells when spatial cues change
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: temporal cues and structure control time cells just as spatial cues and structure control place cells
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the proposal that follows is to treat hippocampal principal neurons as multidimensional rather than as either kind of cell
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: temporal coding is tied to memory three ways: it develops with learning, it is memory-specific, and it predicts judgement accuracy
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A DOUBLE GRADIENT IN MONKEYS: time coding falls and object-identity coding rises going from entorhinal to perirhinal to inferotemporal cortex
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: QUALIFICATION ON THE CROSS-SPECIES CLAIM: the human patterns are slowly changing rather than punctate, closer to an earlier rat result than to the rodent time cells
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: place-cell sequences replay in compressed form during sleep and quiet wakefulness, so spatial coding is recapitulated temporally
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: when spatial and sequence strategies compete, the firing sequences follow whichever strategy the animal expressed on that probe trial
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: FOUR ARGUMENTS AGAINST STRICT CHAINING, first: the cells changed their firing patterns even during the initial part of the delay, rather than simply adding cell activations during the extended segment
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: second: strict chains cannot split to encode overlapping memories that share identical events
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: third: scalar firing is inconsistent with uniform-duration chain activations and consistent with the scalar temporal context model
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: fourth: compressed replay would need a mechanism that can decompress back to the original intervals
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: on the other side, firing chains appear to be preconfigured and then co-opted to organise events
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
